run.change_description: [field] Sync controlled value changes with field state

summary.intent: Make `Field.Control` sync controlled `value` changes through `useValueChanged`, the same mechanism every sibling control (Switch, Checkbox, Select, Slider, Combobox, Number Field, OTP Field) already uses, fixing a dirty-state baseline that never serialized non-string controlled values and a stale filled/dirty/validity state after a programmatic (non-DOM) value change.
summary.issue_fit: No originating issue; intent taken from the pull-request body (supplied as spec text) and verified against it. All four described fixes — the serialized dirty baseline, programmatic-change sync, honoring `details.cancel()`, and controlled DOM changes no longer writing field state directly — are implemented and exercised by new tests that pass at the reviewed head.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff reviewed for both changed files (2/2 diff chunks consumed); callees `useValueChanged`, `useRegisterFieldControl`, `useFieldControlRegistration`, `useFieldValidation` (`commit`/`change`), `createChangeEventDetails`, and `FieldRoot`'s `setDirty`/`markedDirtyRef` wiring were read to confirm effect ordering and the dirty/validate invariants. Focused `FieldControl.test.tsx` run once at the pinned head offline (`TZ=UTC VITEST_ENV=jsdom ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --project @base-ui/react packages/react/src/field/control/FieldControl.test.tsx`): 26 passed, 1 skipped (SSR-only test, skipped under jsdom by design), 0 failed. No verification batch was required: no candidate met a mandatory-verification trigger (must-fix, risk-area, or prior must-fix) and no risk-area or concurrency/failover invariant needed a safety premise.

observations.fact: The PR's own CI performance-benchmark comment reports large regressions (e.g. Menu open +43.9%, Select open +28.5%, Dialog mount +23.0%) for interactions this two-file FieldControl diff does not touch, and a +88B (+0.02%) bundle-size delta.

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/"Dirty state never cleared for non-string values ... The control now registers the serialized value, so the baseline and the comparison agree."
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx (RIGHT): `serializedValue = value == null ? undefined : String(value)` is registered via `useRegisterFieldControl`, so `validityData.initialValue` captures a string baseline instead of a raw number/array. FieldControl.test.tsx (RIGHT) "clears dirty state when a numeric controlled value returns to its initial value" passed at head (vitest: 26 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed).

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/"Programmatic changes left the field stale ... updated the input text but not filled, dirty, or validity"
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx (RIGHT): `useValueChanged(serializedValue, () => { clearErrors(name); setDirty(...); setFilled(...); validation.change(serializedValue); })` fires on any change to the committed controlled value, DOM-driven or not. FieldControl.test.tsx (RIGHT) "syncs state and validates when the controlled value changes programmatically" passed, asserting `data-filled`, `data-dirty`, and one `validate` call with the new value.

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/"`details.cancel()` in `onValueChange` now stops the internal handling. It was ignored."
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx (RIGHT): the uncontrolled `onChange` now captures `details = createChangeEventDetails(...)` and gates `clearErrors`/`validation.change` on `!event.nativeEvent.defaultPrevented && !details.isCanceled`. FieldControl.test.tsx (RIGHT) "does not validate when the change is canceled" passed.

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/"A controlled value the consumer rejects or rewrites no longer reaches the field state, matching Combobox, Number Field and OTP Field."
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.tsx (RIGHT): `onChange` calls `onValueChange?.(inputValue, details)` and then returns immediately when `isControlled`, before any `setDirty`/`setFilled`/`clearErrors`/`validation.change` call, so only the value the consumer actually commits to the `value` prop (observed through `useValueChanged`) can update field state. This mirrors the identical `useValueChanged(value, () => {...})` idiom already used in NumberFieldInput.tsx.

requirements.source: spec-pr5460/"Renders per keystroke for a controlled input ... onSubmit ... 2 on the first, then 1"
requirements.evidence: FieldControl.test.tsx (RIGHT) "renders once per keystroke for controlled input changes" asserts and confirms the default (`onSubmit`) validation-mode steady-state render count at head. The table's `onChange`-mode figure (2 renders per keystroke) has no corresponding test in this diff, so only the tested row is independently verified; nothing in the review depends on the untested figure.
